Phase: Phase 0 — Prerequisites and the consolidation gate
Name: Toolchain installed; evidence model and dated output directories under version control

Phase: Phase 0 — Prerequisites and the consolidation gate
Name: Estate inventory, read-only: the audit seed, the SPN trail and the wider sweep, fused into one inventory

Phase: Phase 0 — Prerequisites and the consolidation gate
Name: Three rationalization lenses applied; consolidation constraints recorded

Phase: Phase 0 — Prerequisites and the consolidation gate
Name: Retain, consolidate or retire, instance by instance
Options (decisions): Retain; consolidate into a target (the source is then retired); retire
If late (decisions): No login may be touched: the audit, Arc and login work all wait on the classified inventory

Phase: Phase 0 — Prerequisites and the consolidation gate
Name: Consolidation target for each consolidated workload
Options (decisions): SQL Server 2022 or 2025 on an Arc-enabled host; Azure SQL Managed Instance; Azure SQL Database or elastic pools. A dedicated target where a constraint blocks shared hosting
If late (decisions): Authentication would be migrated twice, once on the source and again on the target

Phase: Phase 0 — Prerequisites and the consolidation gate
Name: Gate 0 — Consolidation gate passed
Criteria (gates): One row per instance, classified retain, consolidate or retire and justified by the three lenses; a target named for every consolidated workload; collation, vendor-version, compliance-isolation, failover-cluster and dependency constraints recorded; only retain instances and targets go on

Phase: Phase 1 — The authentication audit
Name: Authentication audit of the surviving set: discovery pass, then the deep audit

Phase: Phase 1 — The authentication audit
Name: Audit read: Category 1, 2 or 3 per instance; blockers listed; failover cluster instances flagged

Phase: Phase 1 — The authentication audit
Name: NTLM Phase A baseline: SPN map and collisions, auth_scheme, host Security logs, Restrict NTLM audit policies, enhanced NTLM logging

Phase: Phase 1 — The authentication audit
Name: Upgrade or retire each pre-2022 retain instance
Options (decisions): Upgrade to SQL Server 2022 or later and follow the Category 2-to-1 path; retire or consolidate it; keep it on a sunset-dated exception with the certificate-based interim posture (the authorizing official decides the exception)
If late (decisions): Category 3 instances have no path to Entra logins, and the exception long tail can't be sized

Phase: Phase 1 — The authentication audit
Name: The engine authentication standard
Options (decisions): SQL authentication refused and sa disabled and renamed on every production instance, with break-glass as an empty Windows group; a type-S login kept past migration only as a dated exception with a named compensating control. Open-ended retention isn't an option
If late (decisions): Instances have no standard to cut over against, and the pilot can't be signed off

Phase: Phase 1 — The authentication audit
Name: Gate 1 — Audit read and NTLM baselined
Criteria (gates): Every retain instance and target audited and placed in Category 1, 2 or 3 with its blockers; failover cluster instances treated as Category 3; the Phase A NTLM baseline ingested by compliance monitoring; the authentication standard set

Phase: Phase 2 — The pilot instance
Name: Pilot servers under Arc with machine configuration (program P2.9)
If late (decisions): The pilot SQL Server host has no Arc pattern to follow, and the pilot waits

Phase: Phase 2 — The pilot instance
Name: Pilot host on Arc: egress confirmed, onboarding service principal, managed-identity token validated, SQL Server extension deployed

Phase: Phase 2 — The pilot instance
Name: Graph permissions (SQL Server 2025) or admin consent (SQL Server 2022) granted by a Privileged Role Administrator

Phase: Phase 2 — The pilot instance
Name: Entra authentication on; Entra admin group set; Entra logins and users created beside the Windows ones

Phase: Phase 2 — The pilot instance
Name: Parallel run: 30-day observation, recorded with SQL Server Audit

Phase: Phase 2 — The pilot instance
Name: Disable the superseded Windows logins on the pilot instance
Options (decisions): Disable, don't drop, once the window's exit criteria are met; extend the observation window
If late (decisions): The pilot can't cut over, and the estate waves have no proven pattern

Phase: Phase 2 — The pilot instance
Name: Cutover: Windows logins disabled, not dropped; sa disabled and renamed; scheduled audit started

Phase: Phase 2 — The pilot instance
Name: Gate 2 — Pilot instance on Entra authentication
Criteria (gates): Arc agent Connected; token audience https://database.windows.net/; SQL Server extension Succeeded; Entra admin set; every application and job seen on its Entra login; no remote NTLM rows; no connection arriving only on a legacy Windows login

Phase: Phase 3 — The estate: logins, NTLM restriction, access layer
Name: G1 — Foundation Complete: groups and AUs drift-clean, Conditional Access baseline enforced (program)
If late (decisions): The DBA administrative unit and the SQL group logins have no foundation to build on

Phase: Phase 3 — The estate: logins, NTLM restriction, access layer
Name: DBA administrative unit with restricted management; Groups Administrator scoped to it, eligible through PIM

Phase: Phase 3 — The estate: logins, NTLM restriction, access layer
Name: Access groups and dynamic rules verified; group logins bound; Conditional Access perimeter confirmed on the pilot

Phase: Phase 3 — The estate: logins, NTLM restriction, access layer
Name: Estate waves: every retain instance and target through Arc, Entra authentication, the parallel run and cutover

Phase: Phase 3 — The estate: logins, NTLM restriction, access layer
Name: Phase B, step 1: SPNs registered and collisions repaired, linked-server passthrough replaced, LM and NTLMv1 refused

Phase: Phase 3 — The estate: logins, NTLM restriction, access layer
Name: End dates for legacy authentication and NTLM (program D08)
If late (decisions): Phase B's deny step and the Phase C block have no date to plan against

Phase: Phase 3 — The estate: logins, NTLM restriction, access layer
Name: Move Restrict NTLM from audit to deny, with exceptions from the Phase A baseline
Options (decisions): Deny, with the excepted instances in the domain controller and client lists; stay in audit; if a missed dependency surfaces, relax to audit or add a scoped exception
If late (decisions): NTLMv2 stays open, and Phase C has no restricted baseline to tighten

Phase: Phase 3 — The estate: logins, NTLM restriction, access layer
Name: Phase B, step 2: Restrict NTLM deny settings staged on clients, servers and domain controllers

Phase: Phase 3 — The estate: logins, NTLM restriction, access layer
Name: Gate 3 — Estate on Entra logins, NTLM restricted
Criteria (gates): Every retain instance and target cut over after a clean parallel run; zero critical SPN collisions; Restrict NTLM deny in place with only documented exceptions; DBA administrative unit and group logins verified; a non-compliant sign-in to the SQL resource denied a token

Phase: Phase 4 — The application chain
Name: LDAP-bind inventory over 30 days; each application placed on both axes

Phase: Phase 4 — The application chain
Name: Class and database-axis column for each application
Options (decisions): User axis: Class 3 OIDC, Class 2 SAML, Class 1 Application Proxy, Class 4 Entra Domain Services (last resort). Database axis: A configuration only, B code change, C vendor-dependent, D no Entra path today
If late (decisions): Neither migration track can be sequenced for the application

Phase: Phase 4 — The application chain
Name: Gate conditions prepared: identity holds its database role; change tested on a production-matching Arc stack

Phase: Phase 4 — The application chain
Name: Connection-string cutover, application by application
Options (decisions): Cut over in a change window once all three gate conditions hold; fund the code change (column B); carry a dated exception (columns C and D, and Class 4)
If late (decisions): The application keeps its stored credential, and its host instance can't close

Phase: Phase 4 — The application chain
Name: Connection strings cut over; prior configuration kept; legacy logins disabled, not dropped

Phase: Phase 4 — The application chain
Name: Exceptions filed for Class 4 and deferred applications, sunset dates reconciled against the NTLM block

Phase: Phase 4 — The application chain
Name: Gate 4 — Application chain on Entra principals
Criteria (gates): Every application in Classes 1 to 3 connects as its Entra principal, with no NTLM or KERBEROS rows; every Class 4 or deferred application's host instance carries a dated exception; no stored secret left in a production connection string outside a documented exception

Phase: Phase 4 — The application chain
Name: AD-bound service principal names migrated, retired or islanded (program P4.6)
If late (decisions): SQL Server's applications still hold Windows-authenticated connections when the program measures AD authentication for G4

Phase: Phase 5 — Elimination, closure and the long tail
Name: Certificate audit; SQL Server's three AD CS dependencies mapped; CA-migration order derived

Phase: Phase 5 — Elimination, closure and the long tail
Name: Replacement CA and the AD CS decommission date for SQL Server's certificates
Options (decisions): Book 07's issuers: the retained AD CS hierarchy through CyberArk Certificate Manager, moving to a standalone AD CS issuing CA under the same root when the forest retires; Microsoft Cloud PKI, which would need another enrollment path for SQL Server hosts. Either way, no decommission date until the replacement is issuing
If late (decisions): No decommission date can be set, and the certificate-based interim posture has no assured issuer

Phase: Phase 5 — Elimination, closure and the long tail
Name: Phase C rule for instances whose interim posture isn't in place
Options (decisions): The Phase C date holds for them; dated exceptions with network-level isolation
If late (decisions): The long tail has no rule on the block date, and its exceptions can't be closed

Phase: Phase 5 — Elimination, closure and the long tail
Name: Validation period: closure records and the six evidence sets live and satisfied; drift treated as a violation

Phase: Phase 5 — Elimination, closure and the long tail
Name: Phase C: Restrict NTLM set to deny across the estate

Phase: Phase 5 — Elimination, closure and the long tail
Name: Gate 5 — Estate closed
Criteria (gates): All five closure conditions hold at once on every production instance; the six evidence sets satisfied across the validation period; every excepted instance in the registry with its justification, sunset date and own closure record; the scheduled audit still running

Phase: Phase 5 — Elimination, closure and the long tail
Name: Exception long tail: pre-2022 and Class 4 instances upgraded, re-platformed or retired by their sunset dates
